svg.title: The four advanced retrieval techniques compared on cost and engineering overhead
svg.desc: A hand-drawn matrix comparing GraphRAG, late-interaction retrieval, text-to-SQL, and long-context loading on what each fixes, its offline cost, its online cost, its engineering overhead, and when to ship it. GraphRAG fixes multi-hop joins but needs an LLM-heavy pass over the whole corpus and is only as good as its entity extraction. Late interaction fixes recall on short answer spans but stores one vector per token, growing the index by roughly the tokens per chunk. Text-to-SQL fixes questions whose source is a table, costs nothing offline beyond a schema-docs corpus, and needs only a validation pass and a read-only role. Long-context loading fixes whole-document questions, has no offline cost, pays for the document in full on a cache miss, and is the lowest-engineering option. Captions note text-to-SQL is the cheapest and most-skipped, and that the two graph and token-level techniques are next-iteration work rather than first builds.
svg.text: The deciding information is spread across four sections. Lined up, three of the four are clearly not first builds.
